decisions.rationale: Valid. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r1 on a scratch copy of the lab at 38cb7c1d (lab.json sha256 27501ca9) with one 26/26 solution of its own plus a second passing form of it (different start command, handler class, inline timeout and push condition); the private overlays were not read and LAB_PROJECT; the shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The starter run prints the test 3, 7, 23 and 24 messages the critic cites (tests/lab.mjs lines 198, 248, 398 and 491), test 21's title is printed on every run and in expected/starter-summary.txt line 21, the Dockerfile TODO (starter/reviews/Dockerfile lines 4-5) and the main.py docstring (lines 33-34) are read before phase 5, and README line 106 is read in phase 6 before phase 7. Each of the six named worksheet items (decisions.yaml lines 62, 66, 87, 90, 93 and 97) is therefore decided or reduced to one option by text the learner sees before answering, and for secrets-in-ci#o2 no tested part is left for the page (see ops-edu-11). Acceptance: for each of the six items, no text the learner reads before answering it (starter comments and docstrings, the README, test titles, and every failure message printed by the shipped starter or by the README's end-of-S38 checkpoint state) states its expected option or leaves it as the only option consistent with that text. Messages and comments keep naming the rule to fix but point to the page section instead of stating the page's conclusion; alternatively an item is re-aimed at a case those texts do not decide. Retitling test 21 also changes lab.json failingTests, tests/decisions.test.mjs and both expected/ summaries, which change together. The README phase 6 fork note may stay as a pointer to the secrets page's fork rule without stating what fork runs receive, which still satisfies ops-sme-013's note route, or move after phase 7. An independent critic verifies this by replaying the starter and checkpoint runs. Wording only; no learner time is added.

Valid; same defect as ops-sme-r1-01, and one acceptance covers both. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r1 on a scratch copy of the lab at 38cb7c1d (lab.json sha256 27501ca9) with one 26/26 solution of its own plus a second passing form of it (different start command, handler class, inline timeout and push condition); the private overlays were not read and LAB_PROJECT; the shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. Each of these one-change variants of the reconciler's solution passes 26/26: the 401 guard's body replaced by a print; the guard's HTTPException created without raise; the guard returning an ordinary dict; the guard removed and the headers argument made conditional on authorization so no header is sent and no 401 is answered; and a forwarding dict built but not passed, with the call sending an empty headers dict. tests/lab.mjs lines 273-279 match the guard and the forward as text anywhere, and line 279 counts the conditional-expression form as a guard. Acceptance: reviews-auth-forward fails all five variants above; it passes a guard on missing authorization whose body raises HTTPException with 401 before the outgoing call, with the forwarded value reaching the call either as a dict literal inside its headers argument or through the name assigned that dict or subscript and passed as headers; either header-key case passes; a required authorization header parameter with no guard still passes; and when a guard exists but does not raise, the message names the missing raise. Grader and message change only; no learner time is added.

Valid. The reconciler recomputed, from tests/lab.mjs and starter/decisions.yaml, the expected option's position in the twelve single-question option lists (decisions.yaml lines 14, 16, 25, 50, 55, 61, 69, 82, 86, 89, 92 and 102) and confirms one simple position rule holds in all twelve; with four two-option and eight three-option lists its chance under uniform placement is about 0.2 percent. The positions and the rule are kept out of this record. Acceptance: each single question's expected option is placed by a seeded shuffle whose seed and resulting positions stay in private staging; in the public worksheet, every position that exists in these lists (first, second and, where present, third) holds the expected option in at least two of the twelve lists and in no more than six; the store_contrast blocks keep their per-block ordering from ops-edu-09; the next critic recomputes this from the public tests. Reordering only; no learner time is added.

Valid. coding-lab-timing.json worstRequiredBasis (line 76) is typical 56 plus exactly the four one-minute reruns that reach 60, README line 33 calls it the worst case, and the decide-* rules report only the first wrong field per run (firstWrong, tests/lab.mjs lines 512-517), so four slips anywhere in the 41 worksheet fields use the whole allowance. The record already says no human was timed. Under the operator's bound (typical about 55, worst no more than 60) the fix must not add learner tasks. Acceptance: (1) the README and coding-lab-timing.json describe the 60-minute figure as the typical path plus a stated allowance of four failed reruns at about a minute each, a planning bound and not a measured or derived worst case, and keep the not-observed note; (2) recommended, not binding: each decide-* rule reports every wrong field of its section in one run, so one rerun repairs a whole section; if this is done, no reread hint may state or single out its field's expected option, because every hint then prints on the first starter run (ops-edu-r1-01). Wording change for (1); no learner time is added.

Valid. coding-lab-solved-run.json line 29 describes private solution 1's concrete choices (start command, environment style, timeout object and its arguments, guard, handler order, login technique, basis of the push expression). authoring/schemas/solved-run.schema.json does not forbid this, since runs[].what is free text, but lab-contract.md section 8 (lines 66-71) keeps reference solutions in uncommitted private staging and has validation record only "solved at <commit> by run <id>", authoring/AGENTS.md forbids committing reference solutions, and the operator decision requires that no protected solution material enters Git or reports. None of it is a worksheet answer, but it is a partial description of the reference solution. Acceptance: solution 1's runs[].what is reduced to provenance (who wrote it, that it lives in uncommitted private staging), as solution 2's entry already is; no other entry of the solved-run record describes a private solution's concrete choices beyond what the README and public tests already state; the solved-run record is re-recorded on the new lab bytes and the module lock regenerated. Evidence change only; no learner time.

Valid; same defect as ops-edu-r1-02. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r1 on a scratch copy of the lab at 38cb7c1d (lab.json sha256 27501ca9) with one 26/26 solution of its own plus a second passing form of it (different start command, handler class, inline timeout and push condition); the private overlays were not read and LAB_PROJECT; the shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The critic's four variants reproduce at 26/26 in the reconciler's solution: the guard creating HTTPException without raise, a guard returning a dict, a guard that only prints, and a forwarding dict that never reaches the call while the call sends an empty headers dict. FastAPI documents that HTTPException must be raised (critic evidence). Acceptance: as ops-edu-r1-02. Grader and message change only; no learner time is added.

Valid. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r1 on a scratch copy of the lab at 38cb7c1d (lab.json sha256 27501ca9) with one 26/26 solution of its own plus a second passing form of it (different start command, handler class, inline timeout and push condition); the private overlays were not read and LAB_PROJECT; the shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The reconciler's own env-routed login, wrapped in a run: | block with a trailing backslash before -u, fails both the secret-refs and the no-secret-prints tests (24/26), and the same command with the line break after the pipe fails the same two; the here-string form feeding --password-stdin fails the secret-refs test (25/26). commands() (tests/lab.mjs line 435) splits on every newline, so the feed and the login are judged apart and the no-secret-prints message falsely says a secret is written to the run log. GitHub runs a multi-line run block in one bash -e shell (critic evidence), so these are valid workflow code. Acceptance: before splitting, backslash-newline continuations and a line ending in a pipe are joined with the next line; both wrapped variants above pass both tests; the here-string or redirect form feeding --password-stdin either passes or fails with a message saying the lab expects the piped form; ci-no-secret-prints never reports a secret written to the log for a pipeline that ends in docker login --password-stdin after joining; the ops-sme-005 must-fail cases (literal password, -p and --password forms, login step deleted) still fail. Grader change only; no learner time is added, and it removes a false failure.

Valid. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r1 on a scratch copy of the lab at 38cb7c1d (lab.json sha256 27501ca9) with one 26/26 solution of its own plus a second passing form of it (different start command, handler class, inline timeout and push condition); the private overlays were not read and LAB_PROJECT; the shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. Replacing the reconciler's ConnectError handler with an httpx.HTTPError handler after the TimeoutException handler, same body, fails test 26 (25/26) with the "instead of letting the exception escape" message, although HTTPError is a superclass of ConnectError (critic evidence and its httpx 0.28.1 check) and the handler catches the refused connection. REFUSED (tests/lab.mjs line 305) omits HTTPError while SUPER_OF_TIMEOUT (line 304) includes it. Acceptance: the single refused-connection rule stated in the ops-edu-02 decision of this file; under it, an HTTPError handler placed after the TimeoutException handler and answering a status the page allows for a refused connection passes. Grader change only; no learner time is added.

Valid, low. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r1 on a scratch copy of the lab at 38cb7c1d (lab.json sha256 27501ca9) with one 26/26 solution of its own plus a second passing form of it (different start command, handler class, inline timeout and push condition); the private overlays were not read and LAB_PROJECT; the shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. Removing the top-level permissions block and giving each of the two jobs its own permissions block with only read access to contents fails ci-permissions (25/26) with a request for a top-level block. GitHub documents permissions at the top level or per job (critic evidence); README line 102 and the test title ask only for least access. The secrets page shows the block at the top level, so a README route is also honest. Acceptance: either ci-permissions accepts, when no top-level block exists, a jobs.<job_id>.permissions block on every job under the same read-contents-and-nothing-else rule, or README phase 6 says the block goes at the top level as the secrets page shows; the existing must-fail cases (a string such as write-all, an extra packages write) still fail. Grader or wording change; no learner time is added.

Valid, low. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r1 on a scratch copy of the lab at 38cb7c1d (lab.json sha256 27501ca9) with one 26/26 solution of its own plus a second passing form of it (different start command, handler class, inline timeout and push condition); the private overlays were not read and LAB_PROJECT; the shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. An httpx.Timeout with a None default and explicit connect and read numbers, passed as the call's timeout, fails test 24 (25/26) with the message that a None inside httpx.Timeout turns that limit off and connect and read need real numbers, but connect and read are both explicit numbers there; only the untested write and pool limits are off (critic's httpx 0.28.1 check). Acceptance: either that shape passes when connect and read are explicit numbers, or the message for it says the None default leaves the write and pool limits off; read=None, connect=None and a None default with only connect set still fail. Grader or message change; no learner time is added.

Valid, low. starter/reviews/app/main.py line 4 points to ../tests, which from starter/reviews/app resolves to starter/reviews/tests; that directory does not exist in the lab (the tests are in the lab's top-level tests/ folder). Acceptance: the docstring names the lab's tests folder or gives the correct relative path. A starter byte change, so the starter run, both solved overlays and the critic coverage are re-recorded with the rest of the loop. Wording only; no learner time.

Valid, scoped. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r1 on a scratch copy of the lab at 38cb7c1d (lab.json sha256 27501ca9) with one 26/26 solution of its own plus a second passing form of it (different start command, handler class, inline timeout and push condition); the private overlays were not read and LAB_PROJECT; the shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. A step mapping secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD into env and running base64 with a here-string of that variable passes 26/26, while the echo-piped-into-base64 form fails test 7 as ops-edu-04 required. PRINTERS (tests/lab.mjs line 481) only looks at commands starting with echo, printf, cat, print or tee. secrets-in-ci/artifact.md line 11 opens with exactly this encoded leak, and the ops-edu-04 acceptance names encoded forms such as base64. printenv by name also passes; the first reconciliation's ops-sme-003 decision ruled that case non-binding, and this decision does not change that. Acceptance: ci-no-secret-prints fails a run command that feeds a secret-mapped env variable to an encoder or printer by here-string or redirect (at least the base64 here-string step above, with or without a space after the operator), in addition to the forms it already catches, and the env-context form from ops-edu-04; an ::add-mask:: workflow command and a pipeline ending in docker login --password-stdin are not flagged. A broader rule (any command expanding a secret-mapped variable outside the login pipeline) is acceptable only if its message stays true for every command it flags. Grader change only; no learner time is added.

Still open after loop 1 (education recheck); sharpened acceptance, also closing ops-sme-r1-03. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r1 on a scratch copy of the lab at 38cb7c1d (lab.json sha256 27501ca9) with one 26/26 solution of its own plus a second passing form of it (different start command, handler class, inline timeout and push condition); the private overlays were not read and LAB_PROJECT; the shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. In the reconciler's solution these pass 26/26: (a) the TimeoutException handler widened to a tuple with ConnectError, answering the timeout status, with the old ConnectError handler left below as dead code; (b) an except Exception handler answering 500 placed between the TimeoutException handler and the ConnectError handler; (c) the same with except httpx.HTTPError. The tuple alone, with no separate ConnectError handler, fails with the "letting the exception escape" message although the exception is caught. tests/lab.mjs line 314 takes the refused-connection handler as any later handler naming one of four classes, even when an earlier handler already catches the exception. Acceptance: the refused-connection handler is the first except clause in source order that catches ConnectError, by name, through a superclass (NetworkError, TransportError, RequestError, HTTPError, Exception, BaseException) or as a bare except, including a tuple that contains any of these; that clause must answer a status the service-to-service page allows for a refused connection, or the rule fails with a message about the status. Must fail: variants (a), (b) and (c), and the tuple alone, the last with the status message rather than the escape message. Must pass: a ConnectError, RequestError or HTTPError handler after the TimeoutException handler answering an allowed status (ops-sme-r1-03). The timeout checks already resolved in loop 1 stay: a superclass handler before TimeoutException fails, and swapped statuses fail. Grader and message change only; no learner time is added.

Still open after loop 1 (education recheck); sharpened acceptance. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r1 on a scratch copy of the lab at 38cb7c1d (lab.json sha256 27501ca9) with one 26/26 solution of its own plus a second passing form of it (different start command, handler class, inline timeout and push condition); the private overlays were not read and LAB_PROJECT; the shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. With the trigger reduced to push only, both the starter's unconditional push value and an always-true expression on github.ref pass 26/26, because ci-build-push skips the pull-request case when no pull_request trigger is listed (tests/lab.mjs line 411). The SME recheck of ops-sme-004 counted push: true without a pull_request trigger as valid; the reconciler rules it is not enough for this lab. github-actions-pipeline#o3 asks when an image is only built versus also pushed, which needs a build-only run to exist; the page's workflow triggers on push and pull_request (artifact.md line 17), its cheat sheet says to build on pull requests and push from main (line 97), test 4's own title says the image is pushed only outside pull requests, and the test 1 message already points to the page's on: block. Acceptance: the workflow must also run on pull requests (ci-trigger, or ci-build-push with a message saying so), so the pull-request evaluation always runs and its "a pull request run would push" message is always true; README phase 6 states the behaviour (pull requests are built but not pushed; pushes to main publish) without giving the expression, and the test 1 message names both events by pointing to the page's on: block. Must fail: push-only trigger with an unconditional push; push-only trigger with an always-true github.ref expression; the inverted and always-true forms with both triggers (already failing). Must pass, with both triggers: a push condition on the event name or on the main ref (the page's form among them), an && of event and ref, and a step-level if that skips the step on pull requests around an unconditional push; an unconditional push without such a guard fails, although the SME recheck of ops-sme-004 listed it as valid for a push-only trigger. If test 1 is retitled, lab.json failingTests and both expected/ summaries change with it. Adds one trigger line, well under a minute, inside the phase 6 estimate.

Still open after loop 1 (education recheck); sharpened acceptance. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r1 on a scratch copy of the lab at 38cb7c1d (lab.json sha256 27501ca9) with one 26/26 solution of its own plus a second passing form of it (different start command, handler class, inline timeout and push condition); the private overlays were not read and LAB_PROJECT; the shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The shipped debug step kept with its name, given step env REGISTRY_PASSWORD mapped from secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD and its run text changed from the secrets-context expression to the env-context expression for that variable, passes 26/26. refersTo (tests/lab.mjs line 436) only recognises shell $NAME and ${NAME}. GitHub substitutes an env-context expression into the script text before the shell runs, so the step prints the secret. Acceptance: in ci-no-secret-prints and in ci-secret-refs, the env-context expression for a NAME mapped from secrets is treated as a reference to that secret; must fail: the debug step variant above (ci-no-secret-prints), and an env-context expression of the password variable in the login command (ci-secret-refs, with an accurate message that it writes the value into the command text, as the secrets-context form already gets); must pass: the README's env-routed form with $NAME piped to --password-stdin. The ops-sme-r1-07 encoder rule applies to this form too. Grader change only; no learner time is added.

Still open after loop 1 (education recheck): the README part is fixed (phases 4 and 6 no longer give the Timeout constructor, status codes, needs line, push expression or permissions value), but on the shortest path two declared objectives still have no decisive value derived from their page. The reconciler confirmed the cited texts on the starter run: for secrets-in-ci#o2 the redaction item is stated by the test 7 message (tests/lab.mjs line 491), the derived-value item is named by test 21's title, the fork item is stated by README line 106, and the no-print repair is dictated by the test 7 message; for github-actions-pipeline#o3 the push decision can be skipped (ops-edu-03). Acceptance: (1) ops-edu-r1-01 is met for the three secrets_in_logs items, so at least one secrets-in-ci#o2 worksheet item can be decided only from the secrets page and not from the README, a test title or any starter or checkpoint failure message; (2) ops-edu-03 is met, so the push condition, written by the learner from the pipeline page, is the decisive value for github-actions-pipeline#o3; (3) action SHAs, file names and repair-rule messages that name the rule without its conclusion may stay. The education critic checks every declared objective against the starter run, the end-of-S38 checkpoint run and the README. Wording and grader changes only; no learner time is added beyond ops-edu-03's trigger line.

Still open after loop 1 (SME recheck): part (b) is fixed; part (a) reproduces. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r1 on a scratch copy of the lab at 38cb7c1d (lab.json sha256 27501ca9) with one 26/26 solution of its own plus a second passing form of it (different start command, handler class, inline timeout and push condition); the private overlays were not read and LAB_PROJECT; the shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. A lowercase local named timeout, assigned an httpx.Timeout with a default and a connect limit and never passed, with no timeout on the call, passes 26/26, because the inline check (tests/lab.mjs line 262) matches the assignment statement itself; the same unused local with a plain number as the call's timeout also passes 26/26, although line 264 says a single number is not enough. Acceptance: only a timeout keyword argument inside a call's argument list counts as passing a timeout, for the outgoing httpx call or the httpx client it uses; a statement-level assignment never counts. Must fail: the unused lowercase local with no timeout on the call; the same with a plain number on the call (with the single-number message); an unused Timeout under any other name (already failing). Must pass: an httpx.Timeout passed inline; one bound to a module-level name and passed by that name; one bound to a local named timeout and passed by that name; one passed to an httpx.Client constructor whose client makes the call. Grader change only; no learner time is added.
